answer: Every agent must bind its identity to a dedicated secure-element key and post a slashable bond; auditors randomly issue fresh nonces and slash any pair whose attestation report, key lineage, or hardware measurement matches. A sybil therefore costs real hardware per clone plus lost collateral when duplicates are found, so an attacker buying a thousand fake workers pays for a thousand chips and bonds instead of printing a cheap grove of umber identities around a single oasis.
